text:
The day you love me will have more light than June;

the night you love me will be full moon,

with Beethoven notes vibrating in every ray,

its ineffable things,

and there will be more roses together

than in the whole month of May.


The crystal-clear fountains

will run along the slopes,

leaping crystal-clear

on the day you love me.


The day you love me, the hidden groves

will resound with arpeggios never heard before.

The ecstasy of your eyes: all the springtimes

that have been and will be in the world will be there when you love me.


Holding hands like fair-haired little sisters,

wearing candid collars, the daisies will go

through mountains and meadows,

before your steps, on the day you love me...

And if you pluck one, its innocent

last white petal will tell you: Passionately!


At the breaking of dawn on the day you love me,

all the clovers will have four prophetic leaves,

and in the pond, nest of unknown germs,

the mystic corollas of the lotuses will bloom.


The day you love me, every cloudbank

will be a marvelous wing; every flush of dawn, a mirage

from the Thousand and One Nights; every breeze a song,

every tree a lyre, every mountain an altar.


The day you love me, for the two of us

the beatitude of God will fit inside a single kiss.

translation.title: The Day You Love Me Will Have More Light Than June
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the conditional future, botanical imagery, and the final compression of divine beatitude into one kiss.
